input: There are no competitors. My idea is a form for a student club to collect study-session availability. I observed our organizer chasing answers in a chat yesterday. Please check this possible alternative: https://workspace.google.com/products/forms/ . If you cannot access it, say so and request pasted material. What else might people do?
output:
**Established:** You watched (directly observed) your club's organizer chasing people for availability answers in a chat yesterday — that's a real, recent, observed instance, not hypothetical. You're proposing a form to collect study-session availability.

**Still unknown:** Whether the organizer's frustration was a one-off or recurring, how big your club actually is, how many members you could reach this week, and what the club is *already* using (the chat itself might be the workaround, not a gap).

I fetched the Google Forms page — it loaded fine, no need to paste anything. Quick note before the details: **you don't actually have "no competitors" here** — I want to flag that plainly rather than let it sit unchallenged. Google Forms exists and is free; and more relevantly, there are tools built *specifically* for group availability (not generic surveys) — When2Meet and Doodle. And your club's current group chat *is itself a competing method*, even if a bad one — that's the thing your form has to beat, not "nothing."

**Alternatives researched:**

| Source | Accessed | Target user | Offering | Narrow claim the source supports |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [workspace.google.com/products/forms](https://workspace.google.com/products/forms/) | 2026-09-07 | General (individuals, schools, businesses) | Generic form/survey builder with charts + Sheets export | It's a form builder — the page itself does **not** mention scheduling/availability-grid features (vendor's own description) |
| [doodle.com](https://doodle.com/en/when2meet/) | 2026-09-07 | Groups scheduling a meeting | Propose time slots, participants vote yes/no/maybe, calendar sync, reminders, mobile apps | Vendor claims it handles multi-person scheduling with calendar integration (vendor's own claim about itself) |
| When2Meet (via [meetergo.com summary](https://meetergo.com/en/magazine/when2meet)) | 2026-09-07 | Groups needing a quick free time-grid | Free, no-login drag-to-select grid, color heatmap of overlap | Third-party comparison claims it's free/simple but has no calendar sync, no reminders, no app |

So "what else might people do" — based on this limited search (I only checked these three, I haven't looked at e.g. Calendly, shared spreadsheets, or campus-specific tools), the realistic alternatives are: the group chat itself, a generic Google Form, or a purpose-built poll tool like When2Meet/Doodle. I can't say "nobody does this" — I just haven't found a club-specific tool yet.

A few questions to keep moving:

1. Was the organizer's chasing-answers frustration something you saw *them* directly express (their own experience), or are you inferring it from watching the chat messages go unanswered?
2. Roughly how many people are in this club, and how many could you realistically message and get a reply from before a hackathon judging deadline?
3. Today, before any form, what does the club actually use to nail down study-session times — is it just the raw group chat, or is there already a spreadsheet/poll link floating around?
4. Have you (or the organizer) looked at When2Meet or Doodle already, or would adopting one of those instead of building your own be a fair comparison to test against?
